newsitem.title: USA: Some 15 percent of U.S. children uninsured - study.
newsitem.headline: Some 15 percent of U.S. children uninsured - study.

text.p: About 10 million American children, or almost 15 percent, do not have health insurance, and among Hispanics, almost one-in-three lacks health coverage, a study showed on Thursday.

Uninsured children often end up in the most expensive medical facilities, such as hospital emergency rooms, the American Hospital Association said in releasing statistics compiled by the Employee Benefits Research Institute (EBRI) based on 1994 data.
"The risks that children without health insurance face are different from those of uninsured adults," the hospital association said.

"Children have unique developmental needs, which require greater access to preventive services, such as vaccinations, 'well-baby' care, and diagnostic screening for childhood disorders to ensure that they develop into healthy adults."

Although the national average was 14.4 percent of childen lacking insurance, the rate in at least 13 states was higher. And in California, Oklahoma and Arizona, one-in-five childen was uninsured. In New Mexico and Texas, it was one-in-four.
The states with the lowest non-insurance rates were Wisconsin, at 6.3 percent, and Vermont, 5.5 percent.

Uninsured children do not necessarily have unemployed parents. Many come from working families with low-paid jobs and few benefits. Children in families earning 100 to 150 percent of the poverty level are actually more likely to be uninsured than those below the poverty level, who may qualify for Medicaid.
